themes.note: Frontmatter carries dark values; each colorMeta entry carries its light value. Dark is set on <html> and a visitor's choice is stored in localStorage.theme.

ground.usage: Page background; header at 80% with blur; interchange centre.

panel.usage: Bordered panels, inline code, open station dots, secondary hover.

hairline.usage: Every divider, panel border and table row.

hairline-strong.usage: Secondary-button border, table header rule, quiet side tracks.

ink.usage: Headings, emphasis, primary-button fill, interchange outline.

ink-muted.usage: Leads, metadata, unposted stations, mono labels.

accent.usage: Link hover, focus ring, selection. Never a fill.

code-ground.usage: Fenced code blocks; dark in both themes.

glow.usage: Radial light above each masthead only.

narrative.overview:
The site draws one platform's modernization as a transit network. Every migration is a station on one of six coloured lines (Runtime, Data, Platform, Operations, Security, Team), and every line runs into a single interchange: today's multi-tenant SaaS platform. The map is the memorable thing; everything else exists to get a reader into a post and through it.

The network is now rendered quietly, in the register of Linear and Vercel. The first rendition (navy sign bands, a yellow departure board, condensed signage type) read as dated, so the world keeps its map and drops its paint. Dark is the default theme: a near-black ground, hairline borders, quiet bordered panels, Geist set tight, and a faint light falling from above each page masthead. The map sits in a panel on a plotted dot grid. The six line colours are the only saturated colour anywhere, and they always mean a line.

Density is calm and editorial: generous section spacing, a 1120px container, one column of reading text at about 700px. The world rejects heavy colour fields, shadows as decoration, neon accents and the hero-plus-card-grid template.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first near-black ground with a light theme that swaps tokens, not structure
Hairlines (1px) and 12px bordered panels instead of colour bands or shadows
Six categorical line colours as the only saturation on a page
Thin 3px rails, 9px station dots, a hairline interchange pill
Geist for everything readable; Geist Mono only for code and data labels
One authored motion: the hovered line comes forward and the rest dim

rules.name: The Line Colours Are Data Rule
rules.body: The six line colours are categorical: each one means its line and nothing else. They are the only saturated colour on any page. Never use one as a decorative accent, a button fill or a section background, and never introduce a seventh saturated hue.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from 1px hairlines and quiet bordered panels, not from colour fields. No full-bleed colour bands, no tinted section backgrounds; the masthead glow is the only gradient and it stays below 10% opacity.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only for code and for data labels: dates, read times, column heads, table headers. Never for headings, buttons, navigation or prose, and never uppercase-tracked as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. The only box-shadow in the system is the station ring, and it appears only as a response to hover, focus or "you are here".

rules.name: The Filled Station Rule
rules.body: A filled dot is a station with a post and is a link; an open dot (panel-coloured centre) is a station without one. Never fill a dot that does not lead to a post.

rules.name: The Interchange Is Today Rule
rules.body: Every line runs into one interchange, and it means the present: today's multi-tenant SaaS platform. It is drawn in ink, never in a line colour, and every line ends there; nothing sits beyond it.

rules.name: The Done Work Rule
rules.body: The map shows only finished work. No dashed track, no planned stations, nothing about what comes next.

rules.name: The One Arrow Rule
rules.body: Every directional cue is the same inline SVG arrow (`Arrow.astro`: square caps, miter joins, stroke 3, 1em), rotated for "back". No text-glyph arrows, chevrons or second icon set for direction.

dos: Do treat each line colour as data: use it only where its line is meant (rails, dots, bullets, a post's own markers and TOC).
Do fill a station dot only when that station links to a post; leave it open otherwise.
Do run every line into the single "Today" interchange, drawn in ink, and end it there; the map shows what was done, never what is planned.
Do build structure from 1px hairlines and 12px bordered panels on the near-black ground.
Do use the one SVG arrow (`Arrow.astro`, square-ended, stroke 3) for every directional cue, flipped for "back".
Do keep the primary button for LinkedIn; everything else is secondary or a plain muted link.
Do keep dark as the default and change themes by swapping tokens only.
donts: Don't add colour bands, tinted sections, sign-style navy headers or a yellow board; that was the first rendition and it read as dated.
Don't introduce a saturated colour outside the six lines, or use a line colour as decoration.
Don't use Geist Mono for headings, buttons, navigation or uppercase eyebrows.
Don't add shadows to panels, buttons or cards; the station ring is the only one.
Don't use text-glyph arrows (→, ›) or a second icon style for direction.
Don't let anything scroll horizontally at 320px.
